content: Healthcare professionals should ensure the provision of educational materials that are culturally tailored for patients who do not speak English. These materials should specifically focus on diabetes prevention and awareness, addressing the unique needs of these populations. The National Standards for Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services (CLAS) provide detailed guidance on how to reduce language barriers in healthcare settings. These standards emphasize the importance of improving cultural competency among healthcare providers, ensuring access to language assistance services, and ultimately enhancing the quality of care delivered to individuals who are not proficient in English.
